rationale: Both prior blocking findings are resolved and verified against current source: CR-001's _add_code_tools now gates only the standard call on deselection while the V2-filtered call runs unconditionally (matching AC9/spec D1), with tests updated accordingly; CR-002's migration now backfills '[]' into both tables for pre-existing NULL rows, and every propagation site adds an 'or []' guard as defense in depth. No new findings were discovered; new-scope discovery is out of this targeted verifier's remit.

findings.title: V2 tool variant wrongly suppressed by deselection
findings.problem: _add_code_tools ANDs the deselection check into the same condition that gates the V2 'with filtering' variant.
findings.impact: Violates spec D1/AC9: the V2 variant must stay unaffected by deselecting the standard tool name.
findings.recommendation: Split the condition: gate only the standard call on the deselection check; keep the V2-filtered call unconditional.

findings.title: Missing backfill crashes/bypasses deselection for legacy assistants
findings.problem: The migration added the column as nullable with no backfill, so pre-existing rows load as None.
findings.impact: Unguarded 'in'/'not in' checks at chat time would raise, and the direct-invoke gate would silently no-op for legacy rows.
findings.recommendation: Backfill existing rows to '[]' in the migration; guard every consumer with 'or []' as defense in depth.

finding_status.notes: _add_code_tools now splits standard vs V2 gating; V2 call unconditional on deselection, verified at toolkit_service.py:1604-1646. Tests updated to assert V2 unaffected.

Migration backfills '[]' for both tables (lines 27-33); every propagation site in assistant_version_service.py, assistant_version_migration_service.py and toolkit_service.py adds 'or []' guards as defense in depth.
